content: 1. Rilpivirine increases the risk of toxicity when co-administered with vandetanib due to QTc interval prolongation. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes, as it can exacerbate this risk. 3. Co-administration of voclosporin and rilpivirine can mutually enhance their effects by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Voriconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dose adjustment for rilpivirine is required, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Rilpivirine also increases the toxicity of voriconazole via QTc interval prolongation. 5. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vorinostat, ziprasidone, and other drugs with a known risk of Torsades de Pointes by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 7. Crizotinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval, but the clinical significance is unclear. Monitor closely. 8. Co-administration of rilpivirine with adagrasib significantly increases the risk of QTc interval prolongation, Torsades de Pointes, and other serious arrhythmias. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended. 9. Albuterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Alfuzosin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Aluminum hydroxide decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 12. Amiodarone toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Amisulpride and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration is unavoidable. 14. Amitriptyline toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Amoxapine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Anagrelide and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 17. Apomorphine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Arformoterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Aripiprazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Arsenic trioxide toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Artemether and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 22. Artemether/lumefantrine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Asenapine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Asenapine transdermal and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 26. Atazanavir increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect protease inhibitor levels. 27. Atidarsagene autotemcel should not be co-administered with antiretroviral therapy (ART), including rilpivirine, as ART may interfere with cell manufacturing. Discontinue ART at least 1 month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 28. Atomoxetine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Azithromycin toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Bedaquiline and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 31. Betibeglogene autotemcel should not be co-administered with ART, including rilpivirine, as ART may interfere with cell manufacturing. Discontinue ART at least 1 month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 32. Buprenorphine (all forms) and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 33. Calcium acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 34. Calcium carbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 35. Calcium chloride decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 36. Calcium citrate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 37. Calcium gluconate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 38. Calcium/vitamin D decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 39. Carbamazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. 40. Ceritinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 41. Chlorpromazine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Cimetidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 43. Ciprofloxacin toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Citalopram toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Clarithromycin increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine also increases clarithromycin toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Clomipramine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Clozapine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Conivaptan increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Crizotinib increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Cyclobenzaprine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Dasatinib toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Degarelix toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Desflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 54. Desipramine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Deutetrabenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Certain conditions may increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes or sudden death. 56. Dexamethasone decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. 57. Dexlansoprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. 58. Didanosine and rilpivirine interact via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
